olivia: Quick heads-up — the python sampleapp for embed+rerank is returning different response shapes between sync and async clients. Sync returns a list of dicts under 'items' but async is returning a dict with separate 'embeddings' and 'scores'. I hit this on v0.9.2 when porting a sample app to async. Anyone seen this?
ken: Yep saw something similar after upgrading. The typings for AsyncEmbedReranker still say -> List[RerankResult] but at runtime it spits out Dict[str, Any]. Makes downstream code blow up.
sasha: Can you paste a tiny repro snippet and which sample app?
olivia: Repro (super tiny):
```python
# sync
resp = client.embeddings.rerank(input=["query"], candidates=["a", "b"])
# resp -> [{'score': 0.92, 'embedding': [...], 'candidate': 'a'}, ...]

# async
resp = await client.async_embeddings.rerank(["query"], ["a", "b"])
# resp -> {'embeddings': [[...], [...]], 'scores': [0.92, 0.1]}  # mismatch
```
ken: Looks like the batching helper used for async returns a compact dict (embeddings + scores) to avoid lots of small objects, but we never normalized the public client return shape. Typings/SDK surface didn't get updated.
elaine: Filed DEVEX-412 to track this parity bug and typing mismatch. Likely fix: normalize async client to match sync shape, update type hints, and add unit/integration tests in sampleapp.
devex-bot: New ticket created: DEVEX-412 — Embed/rerank async response shape parity. Assignee: @elaine.
sasha: One more thing I noticed — when token refresh happens mid-batch in async flows, ordering can get shuffled because of how retries are applied in the batch helper. Might be related. Added a note to DEVEX-412.
olivia: Thanks — for immediate unblock I hacked a small normalizer: 
```py
def normalize_rerank(resp):
    if isinstance(resp, dict) and 'embeddings' in resp:
        return [ { 'score': s, 'embedding': e } for s,e in zip(resp['scores'], resp['embeddings']) ]
    return resp
```
I'll open a PR with that + tests. cc @ken for review.
ken: Sounds good. Also propose adding a tiny sampleapp integration test that runs sync vs async path and asserts identical shapes + ordering. Happy to pair on the test.
elaine: I'll pick the ticket up this week. If anyone wants to help with the typing stubs and changelog note ping me.
olivia: Awesome, thanks team :thumbsup:
